messages.content: I have another work trip to arrange. The quality-systems conference in Philadelphia runs Monday, September 18 through Wednesday, September 20, and starts at 9:00 Monday. Then I have a supplier meeting near Newark Thursday morning that should end around noon. I need to leave San Francisco Sunday and return Thursday. Please compare flying home from Philadelphia with flying from Newark, including how I would get between the cities.

I’ll price this as a four-night trip: three nights in Philadelphia and Wednesday night near Newark. Before I compare complete routings, is the supplier site closer to downtown Newark or Newark airport, and do you need to be there at a particular time Thursday?
It is in the airport area, about fifteen minutes from EWR, and I need to arrive by 8:15 a.m. I would rather not drive in Philadelphia unless a car clearly improves the trip.

The cleanest Sunday arrival is American’s nonstop from SFO at 8:05 a.m., reaching PHL at 4:31 p.m., currently $428 in economy. A less expensive Delta itinerary leaves at 7:10 a.m., connects in Minneapolis, and reaches PHL at 5:54 p.m. for $361. The nonstop gives you more recovery time before the 9:00 a.m. conference start. I’ll compare Thursday returns from EWR and PHL around those arrivals.

Use the nonstop as the working outbound. What do the two return choices look like? I can leave for the airport shortly after the meeting, but noon is an estimate, so do not make the connection too tight.

Returning from EWR, United has a nonstop at 3:35 p.m., arriving SFO at 6:45 p.m. The open-jaw fare paired with the American outbound is $612 total. A 5:10 p.m. United nonstop arrives at 8:22 p.m. and brings the airfare to $584. Both leave adequate time after a noon finish; the later one has substantially more margin. Returning from PHL, American has a 5:40 p.m. nonstop arriving SFO at 8:43 p.m. for $548 total, but you would need to travel back from the Newark area after the meeting.
Please lay out the timing for that Philadelphia return. Also compare train plus local transportation with renting a car Wednesday.

For the 5:40 p.m. PHL flight, I would target leaving the supplier by 12:30 p.m. A car from the Newark airport area to PHL is roughly 85 to 120 minutes in ordinary Thursday traffic, but delays can be materially worse; rental return and security make that option uncomfortable. By rail, you would take NJ Transit from Newark Airport station to Newark Penn, Amtrak to 30th Street, then the airport line to PHL. Even with a 1:05 p.m. Amtrak departure, the sequence reaches the airport around 3:15 p.m. if each connection works. It is feasible, but the fare savings do not compensate for the backtracking and connection risk.
Agreed. Keep the EWR return options. Now compare getting to Newark Wednesday evening by Amtrak and rideshare versus picking up a car in Philadelphia after the conference.

The rail plan is straightforward: depart Philadelphia 30th Street at 5:59 p.m. on Amtrak, arrive Newark Penn at 7:04 p.m., then take a rideshare to the airport hotel. A flexible Amtrak fare is $68, and the two Newark-area rideshares should total about $62: hotel Wednesday evening and supplier-to-EWR Thursday. Allowing $18 to reach 30th Street from the conference area, intercity and local transportation totals about $148. A one-way midsize rental picked up near 30th Street at 5:00 p.m. and returned at EWR Thursday is $176 including taxes, before fuel, parking, and tolls; the practical total is about $229. Rail is both less expensive and avoids the one-way drive.

Use rail in the working plan. I need hotels next. The conference block only has rooms through Wednesday morning. Compare that with nearby refundable public rates that let me stay through Wednesday checkout, then give me practical Newark airport choices for Wednesday night.

For Philadelphia, the conference hotel is the Philadelphia Marriott Downtown, directly connected to the convention center. The block is available Sunday through Tuesday nights at $259 nightly; with taxes, three nights total $912.48. It is refundable until 6:00 p.m. local time on September 14. A public flexible rate at the same hotel is $1,047.66 for the same three nights and cancels until 11:59 p.m. September 16. The nearby Hilton Garden Inn is $846.27 total, about a four-minute walk, with cancellation until 11:59 p.m. September 15. All three allow Wednesday checkout; the block limitation means you cannot add Wednesday night, which you do not need because you are moving to Newark.
That makes the block sound reasonable. Is there any practical drawback besides the earlier cancellation deadline? And what is available at Newark?

The block’s main drawbacks are the September 14 cancellation cutoff and a one-night charge for later cancellation. Otherwise it is the most convenient Philadelphia option and costs $133.79 less than the flexible public rate at the same property. Near EWR, the Newark Liberty International Airport Marriott is $287.41 for Wednesday night, refundable until 6:00 p.m. September 19, with a 24-hour airport shuttle. The Hampton Inn Newark Airport is $214.36, refundable until 11:59 p.m. September 19, with breakfast beginning at 6:00 a.m. and a scheduled airport shuttle. The Renaissance Newark Airport is $236.18, refundable until 6:00 p.m. September 20, but its shuttle goes only to the airport terminals, not the supplier site.

The airport Marriott is probably easiest, but check the Thursday morning logistics. I need to be at the supplier by 8:15 and will have luggage. Can the hotel hold it after checkout, or should I take it to the meeting?

The Marriott can hold luggage after checkout, but retrieving it after a noon meeting would add a stop before the flight. With the supplier only about fifteen minutes away, the simpler sequence is to check out around 7:35 a.m., take your luggage in the rideshare, and ask the supplier to store it during the meeting. A 7:40 departure provides roughly twenty minutes of buffer for an 8:15 arrival. After the meeting, a direct rideshare to EWR should take about fifteen minutes.
That works. Price the complete trip with the Marriott block in Philadelphia, the airport Marriott Wednesday, rail, and each EWR flight. Include the ground estimates so I can compare actual totals.

With the 3:35 p.m. EWR departure: airfare $612.00, Philadelphia Marriott block $912.48, Newark Airport Marriott $287.41, Amtrak and local rideshares $148.00, for a projected total of $1,959.89. With the 5:10 p.m. departure: airfare $584.00, the same $1,199.89 in lodging, and $148.00 in ground transportation, for a projected total of $1,931.89. The later flight saves $28 and gives you about two additional hours after the meeting.
Is there an earlier train Wednesday that would still let me attend the full final conference day? The last session ends at 4:15, and I may need twenty minutes afterward.

The best earlier-compatible train leaves 30th Street at 5:30 p.m. and reaches Newark Penn at 6:35 p.m. You would need to leave the convention center by about 4:50, so it accommodates the full session and twenty minutes afterward if you use a taxi or rideshare. Its flexible fare is $74, raising the trip total by $6. The 5:59 train gives you more breathing room and reaches the Newark hotel around 7:30 p.m., which is still reasonable for the next morning.
Keep the 5:59 train. Before we narrow this down, compare the Hampton against the airport Marriott in the full total and confirm whether either rate requires prepayment.

Neither quoted rate requires prepayment; each uses a card guarantee and charges at the property. Substituting the Hampton reduces lodging by $73.05. With the 5:10 p.m. flight, the projected complete total becomes $1,858.84 versus $1,931.89 at the airport Marriott. The Hampton has the later cancellation cutoff on September 19, while the Marriott has the shorter shuttle ride and is more convenient if you need airport services Wednesday evening. Because you will use rideshares to and from the supplier either way, the Marriott’s location does not materially simplify Thursday morning.

Then narrow it to the Hampton and the airport Marriott, both refundable, and use the 5:10 return. I am not ready to book because the supplier may shift the meeting by a day. Give me the exact working itinerary and the deadlines I need to watch.

Working itinerary: Sunday, September 17, American nonstop SFO-PHL, 8:05 a.m.-4:31 p.m. Monday through Wednesday, conference at the Pennsylvania Convention Center, with three nights at the Philadelphia Marriott Downtown conference block for $912.48. Wednesday, check out, attend through 4:15 p.m., depart for 30th Street around 5:10 p.m., take the 5:59 p.m. Amtrak to Newark Penn arriving 7:04 p.m., then rideshare to the hotel. Thursday, leave the hotel about 7:40 a.m. with luggage, attend the 8:15 a.m.-approximately noon supplier meeting, rideshare directly to EWR, and take United’s 5:10 p.m. nonstop to SFO, arriving 8:22 p.m. Airfare is $584.00. The Newark finalists are Hampton Inn Newark Airport at $214.36, producing a projected trip total of $1,858.84, and Newark Liberty International Airport Marriott at $287.41, producing a total of $1,931.89. The Philadelphia block must be canceled by 6:00 p.m. local time September 14. The Hampton is refundable through 11:59 p.m. September 19; the airport Marriott through 6:00 p.m. September 19. No flight, rail ticket, or hotel has been booked.
